glossary.Bone marrow: The soft tissue inside bones that makes blood cells.
glossary.Penetrating injury: A wound where an object pierces through the skin into deeper tissue.
glossary.Discharging sinus: A tract from infected tissue to the skin that leaks pus.
glossary.Foot ulcer: An open sore on the foot, common in diabetes from nerve damage and poor circulation.
glossary.IV drug use: Injecting drugs into veins, which can carry bacteria into the blood.
glossary.Long bone: A bone longer than it is wide, such as the femur, tibia or humerus.
glossary.CRP: C-reactive protein, a liver protein that rises quickly in infection and inflammation.
glossary.ESR: Erythrocyte sedimentation rate, a slower, non-specific blood marker of inflammation.
glossary.WBC: White blood cell count; raised in infection.
glossary.Spinal percussion: Tapping over the spine to find a tender, infected vertebra.
glossary.Vertebral osteomyelitis: Infection of the bones of the spine.
glossary.Femoral head: The ball at the top of the thigh bone that sits in the hip socket.
glossary.Humeral head: The ball at the top of the upper arm bone that forms the shoulder joint.
glossary.Chronic osteomyelitis: Long-standing bone infection with dead bone, often needing surgery.
glossary.Pathological fracture: A break through bone already weakened by disease.
glossary.Surgical drainage: Opening an abscess surgically to let the pus out.
glossary.Culture: Growing organisms from a sample in the lab to identify them and test antibiotics.
glossary.Definitive: Final and targeted, rather than a best guess.
glossary.Blood cultures: Blood samples incubated to detect bacteria in the bloodstream.
glossary.MRI: Magnetic resonance imaging; detailed scan of soft tissue and marrow without radiation.
glossary.Sensitive: Good at picking up disease when it is present.
glossary.Cortical: Relating to the hard outer shell of bone.
glossary.Ultrasound: Imaging with sound waves; shows fluid collections well.
glossary.Empirical: Started before the organism is known, based on the most likely cause.
glossary.IV: Intravenous: given directly into a vein.
glossary.Penicillin allergy: An immune reaction to penicillin drugs; flucloxacillin is a penicillin.
glossary.Sensitivities: Lab results showing which antibiotics kill the cultured organism.
glossary.Antimicrobials: Drugs that kill or stop microorganisms, including antibiotics.
glossary.Systemic illness: Whole-body effects of infection such as fever, tachycardia and low blood pressure.
glossary.Seeding: Bacteria in the blood settling and multiplying in a tissue.
glossary.Vascular supply: The blood vessels feeding a tissue.
glossary.Bone matrix: The collagen and mineral framework of bone.
glossary.Penetration: How well a drug reaches into a tissue.
glossary.Immune clearance: Removal of organisms by white cells and antibodies.
glossary.Ischaemia: Inadequate blood supply to a tissue.
glossary.Infarction: Tissue death caused by loss of blood supply.
glossary.Translocation: Bacteria crossing from the gut lumen into the blood.
